- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate early in horizon; reduce forecast peaks, especially in first 5–7 days.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model underestimates true volatility; increase forecast tail risk and lower early values to reflect downward pressure.
- Model often overshoots after sharp sentiment spikes (e.g., sentiment jumps to 1.00), leading to over-optimistic 30d forecasts; apply dampening factor to post-spike values.
- Mean reversion is underemphasized — model fails to correct for recent high sentiment-driven peaks; apply slight downward bias to forecasts if sentiment has been >0.67 for 3+ consecutive days.
- Horizon-specific error: 30d forecasts are too optimistic in early days (1–10) when sentiment is positive; adjust downward by 10–20% for first 5 days if sentiment >0.67.
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows, model fails to capture cyclical mean reversion; apply smoothing filter to forecast series to reduce erratic swings.
